content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Use Would you like to and short acceptance or refusal. Model: “Would you like to walk in the park? Yes, that sounds good.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use would you like to come? clearly and politely. One useful response is: “Would you like to walk in the park? Yes, that sounds good.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where would you like to come? is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?

pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Link would you; use a friendly rise in the invitation. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Link would you; use a friendly rise in the invitation.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about would you like to come?.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using would you like to come?; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise would you like to come??” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: Would you like to walk in the park? Yes, that sounds good.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about would you like to come? with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about would you like to come?. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: Would you like to walk in the park? Yes, that sounds good. Submit your draft first.
